Back in the 1930s, people said your income is the average of your five best friends.

Kevin Trudeau says the reason is simple: those five people are who you listen to, who you watch, and who you spend your time with - so you subconsciously start thinking, talking and acting like them.

Today those five friends aren't just the people in your house. They're whoever is in your YouTube feed, your Instagram, your group chats.

Watch broke people and you'll think broke. Watch wealthy, successful people and your energy starts shifting toward health, wealth and happiness.

Who are your five? Are they building you up, or capping you?

#kevintrudeau #wealthmindset #millionairemindset #successhabits #moneymindset #businessmotivation

Kevin Trudeau grew up around plumbers, welders and union workers - no business owners, no wealthy people to learn from.

So he became a caddy at a country club just to stand near rich members, and later a busboy at the fanciest restaurant in town, just to watch how wealthy people walked, talked and dressed.

He saw the Cadillacs and the Lincolns out front, the Lobster Thermidor on the table, the expensive watches - and wealth stopped being a fantasy. It became something real he could actually see.

You don't need money to start studying money. You need proximity.

#kevintrudeau #wealthmindset #millionairemindset #successhabits #moneymindset #businessmotivation

Aristotle Onassis was once the wealthiest man in the world. Then he lost everything in World War One and escaped to Argentina with only the clothes on his back.

Kevin Trudeau says the one thing Onassis knew was that he had to be in the same physical location as wealthy people again - so he worked as a waiter and a busboy in the restaurants where they ate.

Napoleon Hill called what happens when wealthy people gather in one room a mastermind - a bubble of high-frequency energy that rubs off on whoever is standing in it.

Onassis stood in it on purpose, and rebuilt his fortune.

#kevintrudeau #wealthmindset #millionairemindset #successhabits #moneymindset #businessmotivation

Josh and Matt Altman - the stars of Million Dollar Listing Los Angeles, now sitting on a billion and a half dollars in real estate - started out broke, sharing a one-bedroom apartment.

Kevin Trudeau says they knew one thing: they had to be in the same physical space as wealthy people. So they went to a Beverly Hills bar lined with Rolls-Royces and Ferraris out front, and ordered a single club soda because that's all they could afford.

They sat, they listened, and they left angry every time - if they can do it, why can't we? That anger is what made them start dreaming bigger.

#kevintrudeau #wealthmindset #millionairemindset #successhabits #moneymindset #businessmotivation

Kevin Trudeau says the algorithm is telling you exactly what you're thinking - and you can't hide from it.

He proved it live: pulled up a pool match with his friend Mike Siegel, a ten-time world champion, and checked the recommended videos. The feed was full of Jim Rohn, Les Brown and Shark Tank clips on building wealth.

Check your own feed right now. If it's full of broke people complaining, that's what you're feeding your brain. If it's full of people building wealth, that's a different brain altogether.

Open your app and actually look. What is it telling you about how you think?

#kevintrudeau #wealthmindset #millionairemindset #successhabits #moneymindset #businessmotivation

Kevin Trudeau tells the story of a friend from Boston, thick accent and all, who went away to college in South Carolina for one semester.

He came home for Christmas talking like a local - how y'all doing - without even realizing he'd picked it up. A few months around a Southern accent, and his own Boston accent was gone.

That's exactly how fast you absorb the people around you - their habits, their beliefs, their thinking about money - whether you notice it happening or not.

So who exactly are you letting rewrite your accent?

#kevintrudeau #wealthmindset #millionairemindset #successhabits #moneymindset #businessmotivation

Kevin Trudeau's advice gets uncomfortable fast: follow only wealthy, successful people on social media. Go sit at the bar in restaurants where the rich go, even if all you can afford is a club soda. Join a club where successful people are members.

Then comes the hard part. He says you may have to get rid of some of your current friends and go find new ones, because you become what you think about most of the time - and your thinking is shaped by who you watch, listen to and spend time with.

If you want to change your income and your financial situation, change the room you're in.
